name: Easy Cheesy Scrambled Eggs
pitch: You literally have everything you need for this — eggs and cheese are the whole show, and it's on the table in under 10 minutes.
steps: Crack your eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and pepper, and beat them together. No milk? No problem — skip it or add a small splash of water for a fluffier texture.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium-low heat with a little butter or oil, then pour in the eggs.
Gently stir and fold the eggs as they cook — low and slow is the move here, it keeps them soft instead of rubbery.
When the eggs are just barely set (still look a little wet), scatter in your cheese and fold it in for another minute until melted.
Eat as-is, on toast, or wrapped in a tortilla if you've got one.

name: Pittata – Pizza Frittata
pitch: Think of this as a cheesy baked egg pie — it sounds fancy but it's mostly hands-off, and your eggs and cheese carry it just fine without the extras.
steps: Preheat your oven to 450°F on the top heat (broil) setting, or as close as you can get.
Beat your eggs in a bowl with salt, pepper, and any dried herbs you like — Italian seasoning or oregano would be great here. No milk? Just skip it, it's totally optional.
Heat a little oil or butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat. If you have any veggies around (even frozen ones), toss them in now.
Pour the egg mixture into the skillet and let it spread out evenly. Scatter your cheese generously on top — use whatever you've got, mozzarella, parmesan, cheddar, all of it.
Cook on the stovetop until the edges look set, about 4–5 minutes. The middle will still be a bit jiggly — that's fine.
Slide the whole pan into the oven and bake until the top is puffed and golden, about 5–8 minutes. Watch it closely toward the end.
Let it cool for a couple minutes, then slice into wedges like a pizza.

name: Cream Cheese Deviled Eggs
pitch: If you have cream cheese on hand, this is a fun little twist on deviled eggs — the filling is extra creamy and mild, which makes it a hit with kids.
steps: Place your eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then let them boil for 5 minutes. Take the pan off the heat, cover it, and let the eggs sit in the hot water for 10 minutes.
Transfer eggs to a bowl of cold water to cool — this makes them way easier to peel.
Peel the eggs and slice them in half lengthwise. Pop the yolks out into a small bowl.

Mash the yolks with your cream cheese, a pinch of salt, and a little pepper until smooth and creamy. No ham? That's fine — the cream cheese filling is plenty tasty on its own. A tiny squeeze of mustard or a dash of paprika adds a nice kick if you have it.
Spoon or pipe the filling back into the egg whites. Dust with paprika if you've got it — it makes them look great for almost zero effort.
